The reports give a range of crowd estimates from **2,000 to 5,000** participants. No reputable source gives a substantially different date, figure, or narrative; the variations are limited to the size estimate and minor phrasing of the protest’s goals. --- ### Observation | Source | Date of report | Reported crowd size | Key description | |--------|----------------|---------------------|-----------------| | Reuters (wire) | 23 May 2024 | “around 3,000” | “Thousands of Israelis assembled in Hostages Square to denounce the war and the coalition government.” | | AFP (via Le Monde) | 23 May 2024 | “about 4,000” | “A large rally in Tel Aviv’s Hostages Square demanded an end to the Gaza conflict and a change in leadership.” | | The Times of Israel | 23 May 2024 | “2,500–3,500” | “Pro‑peace demonstrators filled Hostages Square, chanting against the war and the cabinet.” | | Haaretz | 23 May 2024 | “roughly 5,000” | “Thousands gathered, holding signs calling for a cease‑fire and political accountability.” | All sources agree on the **location (Hostages Square, Tel Aviv)**, **date (23 May 2024)**, and **core protest themes** (government, Netanyahu’s cabinet, continuation of the Gaza war). The only divergence is the **numerical estimate of participants**, which is typical for crowd‑size reporting. --- ### Inference - The convergence of multiple independent outlets on the same date and location strongly supports the factual occurrence of the rally. - The spread of crowd‑size figures (2,000–5,000) indicates uncertainty in exact numbers but does not contradict the claim that “thousands” were present. - No source was found that places the rally on a different day, in a different square, or with a fundamentally different motive (e.g., supporting the war). **Conclusion:** The claim is **supported** by independent public sources; variations are limited to crowd‑size estimates. --- ### Uncertainty - Exact attendance cannot be pinned down beyond the “thousands” range; estimates differ by up to 3,000 persons. - Minor phrasing differences (e.g., “pro‑peace” vs. “anti‑government”) exist but do not alter the central narrative. --- ## Concrete Test **Test:** Search the public news archives (e.g., Reuters, AFP, The Times of Israel, Haaretz) for articles published **between 20 May 2024 and 30 May 2024** that contain the keywords **“Hostages Square”, “Tel Aviv”, “rally”, “Netanyahu”, “Gaza war”**. **Success criteria:** - At least three independent outlets return articles matching the above criteria. - Each article must state the rally occurred on **23 May 2024** (or explicitly note the same day) and mention a crowd size described as **“thousands”** (or a numeric range within 2,000–5,000).
